source_detail: Average Effective Tariff Rate — Policy through July 21, 2026 (Pre-Substitution)
title: Average Effective Tariff Rate
subtitle: Policy through July 21, 2026, Pre-Substitution
latest_source: Yale Budget Lab April 8 snapshot + Section 301 Brazil (July 15)
methodology: Each data point is the headline overall pre-substitution average effective US tariff rate produced by the Yale Budget Lab Tariff Rate Tracker. Methodology: Yale applies announced tariff schedules (MFN + Section 122 + Section 232 + Section 301 + any IEEPA authority in effect) at the HTS10 × trading-partner level to ~240 partners and ~20,000 HS10 product codes, weighted by pre-tariff import shares. Stacking rules: MFN is additive in all branches, Section 232 took precedence over IEEPA while IEEPA was in effect, Section 301 is always cumulative. Pre-substitution means the rate applies announced schedules to the pre-tariff import mix without adjusting for consumer/supplier behavioral substitution. Source pipeline: Budget-Lab-Yale/tariff-rate-tracker on GitHub.

notes: Each point through April 8, 2026 is the headline overall pre-substitution 'average effective US tariff rate' reported by the Yale Budget Lab in a 'State of U.S. Tariffs' update. Points after April 8 are policy-event carry-forwards based on Yale's last published snapshot, adjusted for material new tariff actions (Section 301 on Brazil) using Yale's HTS-weighted methodology.

Yale methodology: announced tariff schedules (MFN, Section 122, Section 232, Section 301) are applied at the HTS10 × trading-partner level to ~240 partners and ~20,000 HS10 product codes, weighted by pre-tariff import shares. Pre-substitution means no adjustment for consumer/supplier behavioral shifting. Pipeline open-source at github.com/Budget-Lab-Yale/tariff-rate-tracker.

Key 2025 events: April 2 'Liberation Day' 10% universal baseline, April 9 revised reciprocal rates (peak ~28%), May 12 US-China 90-day pause, May 28 Court of International Trade ruling briefly vacating IEEPA, Federal Circuit stay restoring IEEPA tariffs, August 1 reciprocal tariffs effective, November 2025 agricultural exemptions.

Key 2026 events: January 19 Greenland tariffs (+17.5%), February 20 SCOTUS vacates IEEPA tariffs (rate drops to 9.1%), February 24 Section 122 10% surcharge takes effect (150-day authority), April 2 Section 232 metals restructuring + pharma 100% (phased in), May 7 CIT invalidates Section 122 (stayed on appeal June 11), July 15 Section 301 25% on Brazil.

UPCOMING: Section 122 10% surcharge expires July 24, 2026 (3 days). If not replaced, rate drops ~4pp to ~7-8%. USTR has proposed 10-12.5% Section 301 tariffs on 46 countries as a replacement (hearings completed July 20). Section 232 pharma 100% tariff phases in August-October 2026 (120-180 days from April 2 proclamation).

Penn Wharton Budget Model reports a May 2026 effective rate of 7.2% — this uses a different methodology (post-substitution, import-weighted by actual 2026 trade flows rather than pre-tariff baseline). The gap between Yale pre-sub (~12%) and PWBM (~7%) reflects both substitution effects and methodological differences.
